# one-definition-two-apis rule, and the api overload-set ambiguity check:
#
#   Compiled1.i  Compiled2.a  Compiled3.g  Compiled3.q  Compiled5.bq  Compiled5.y
#
# The three the phase-2 api check mode newly REACHED went the same way in the
# same commits: Compiled3.w.fsi, Compiled5.bp.fss, Compiled5.x.fsi. So did four
# that were listed from before: Compiled0.p, Compiled10.g, Compiled3.r and
# XXXPreparser.c.
#
# ONE OF THE SEVEN IS STILL HERE AND IT IS THE LINE BELOW.
#
#   Compiled1.al  "Item at this location must be an expression, not an
#                  operator", at 15:48, which is the `^` in `f(a)^b`.
#                  RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE OPERATOR GRAMMAR after SPIKE-OPEXPR's
#                  declaration half landed: it still compiles and it computes
#                  the RIGHT ANSWER -- `dbl(3)^2` is 81.
#                  The only spec rule that could refuse it is the
#                  superscripted-postfix rule, lexical-structure.tex:1204-1213,
#                  and that rule EXCLUDES this case by its own wording: `^T` is
#                  a postfix operator "provided that it is not immediately
#                  followed by a word character", and `^b` is not a simple
#                  operator preceded by `^` either.
#                  THE BROAD READING THAT WOULD REFUSE IT COSTS 383 SITES ACROSS
#                  103 FILES, six of them inside the compiling set, and they are
#                  overwhelmingly `^2` and `^3`. So the spec supports US and not
#                  the legacy here.
#                  It stays in THIS file and not in the divergence list because
#                  the gate cannot hold an acceptance there -- `verdict` refuses
#                  to reclassify a case whose detail is "ACCEPTED a program",
#                  deliberately. Defect register DEV-12.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
